temperature.title: Alumina cools chamber by chamber
temperature.description: Hot alumina from the calciner/cyclone coolers (several hundred °C) flows through the cascade of fluidised chambers. Fluidising air and the immersed water-cooled bundles remove heat; the water flows counter-current to the alumina. Product leaves at roughly 80 °C or less for safe conveying and storage; the warm air is often used as combustion air.

video_tutorials.title: Calcination Fluidized Bed Cooler — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Calcination Fluidized Bed Cooler.
A fluidised bed cooler cools hot calcined alumina.
The alumina flows through fluidised chambers with immersed water-cooled tube bundles; fluidising air keeps it moving and is warmed for reuse in the calciner.
Typical applications include stationary (gas-suspension / circulating fluid bed) calciner product cooling; cooling other hot granular products (e.g. cement raw materials, catalysts).
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Cooler Body, Air Distributor & Chamber Weirs.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Calcination Fluidized Bed Cooler works.
Hot alumina enters the first chamber.
Air fluidises the bed.
Tube bundles remove heat.
Alumina flows over weirs to the outlet.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Hot alumina from the calciner/cyclone coolers (several hundred °C) flows through the cascade of fluidised chambers.

video_tutorials.title: Calcination Fluidized Bed Cooler — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Calcination Fluidized Bed Cooler.
Check outlet temperature and water flow.
Inspect nozzles and bundles for erosion.
Replace bundles.
Watch for tube leak: wet alumina, steam. Common cause: erosion.
Watch for defluidisation: hot spots. Common cause: blocked distributor.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
